chosen.premise: Gyarados’s rage can last an entire month, ending only after it has burned everything down.
chosen.hook: Gyarados can stay enraged for an entire month.
chosen.visualIdea: A calendar rapidly flips through 30 days while Gyarados’s rampage spreads across a burning map.
chosen.note: A precise, disturbing duration backed directly by the Sapphire entry; the calendar-and-rampage visual makes the premise immediately legible.

candidates.premise: At level 20, Magikarp becomes Gyarados—and its brain cells structurally transform, triggering its violent nature.
candidates.hook: What if evolving at level 20 rewired your brain?
candidates.visualIdea: Show Magikarp hitting level 20, then morph into Gyarados as a brain diagram violently rearranges.
candidates.note: Highly distinctive transformation with strong visual potential, but the claim that the brain change directly triggers violence is presented as speculation in the Pokédex.

candidates.premise: Mega Gyarados keeps the same 6.5-meter height but jumps from 235 kg to 305 kg and becomes Water/Dark.
candidates.hook: Mega Gyarados gets heavier without getting taller.
candidates.visualIdea: Overlay both forms at equal height, then slam a 235 kg counter into a 305 kg counter.
candidates.note: Exceptionally clean numerical comparison with complete support, though the reveal is more stat-focused and less emotionally gripping than Gyarados’s destructive lore.

candidates.premise: In one account, Gyarados fires Hyper Beams in every direction, burning its surroundings to ash.
candidates.hook: Gyarados doesn’t aim one Hyper Beam—it fires everywhere.
candidates.visualIdea: Animate beams exploding outward from Gyarados in a full circle until the landscape becomes ash.
candidates.note: The all-directions detail is concrete and highly animatable, but it comes from a single Pokédex account and may feel like an isolated version-specific claim.

candidates.premise: According to multiple Pokédex accounts, human conflict draws Gyarados out—and the places it reaches are destroyed.
candidates.hook: Human conflict may be the signal that summons Gyarados.
candidates.visualIdea: A small argument on a map escalates into war, then a Gyarados silhouette appears over the burning location.
candidates.note: Multiple entries support Gyarados appearing during conflict, but “summons” implies a stronger causal mechanism than the text establishes.

candidates.premise: Gyarados is Water/Flying, yet its defining attacks and rampages repeatedly burn cities, villages, and fields.
candidates.hook: Why does a Water-type Pokémon keep setting everything on fire?
candidates.visualIdea: Place Water and Flying type labels beside footage-style illustrations of cities and mountains burning.
candidates.note: The contradiction is visually strong, but the evidence mostly describes Hyper Beam and Pokédex lore rather than establishing fire as a defining attack or Water-type paradox.

rounds.request: None; month-long-rampage is strong enough. A stronger alternative would need an equally precise, well-supported fact with a more uniquely Gyarados-specific contradiction or reveal.
